title: Decimals
description: Class 5 IMO — Decimals: thousandths and place value, decimal–fraction conversion, comparing and ordering decimals, and multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 and 1000.

topics.title: Thousandths & Decimal–Fraction Conversion
topics.concept:
The third place after the decimal point is thousandths (0.001 = 1/1000). In 2.345 there are 2 ones, 3 tenths, 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths.

To change a decimal to a fraction, write the digits over 10, 100 or 1000: 0.25 = 25/100 = ¼. To change a fraction to a decimal, make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000: ¾ = 75/100 = 0.75.

examples.problem: Write 0.6 as a fraction in simplest form.

quiz.q: In 4.567, the digit 7 is in the ___ place.
quiz.explanation: The third digit after the point is thousandths.

quiz.q: Write 0.5 as a fraction in simplest form.

topics.title: Comparing & Ordering Decimals
topics.concept:
To compare decimals, line them up by place and compare the whole numbers first, then tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. Adding zeros helps: 0.5 = 0.50.

So 0.5 is greater than 0.45, and to order 0.3, 0.33 and 0.303 from least we write 0.3, 0.303, 0.33.

examples.solution: 0.5 = 0.50, and 50 hundredths > 45 hundredths, so 0.5 is bigger.

recap: Compare wholes, then tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
Add zeros to give the same number of places (0.5 = 0.50).

quiz.explanation: Adding a zero at the end does not change the value: 0.250 = 0.25.

topics.title: Multiplying & Dividing by 10, 100, 1000
topics.concept:
Multiplying a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000 moves the decimal point to the right by 1, 2 or 3 places. Dividing moves it to the left by 1, 2 or 3 places.

So 2.5 × 10 = 25, and 45 ÷ 100 = 0.45.

examples.solution: Move the point one place right: 25.
Move the point two places left: 0.45.

quiz.explanation: Move the point two places right: 340.
Move the point three places left: 0.25.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three are equal to ¼)?
questions.explanation: 0.025 is 25 thousandths, not a quarter; the other three equal ¼.
The third decimal place is thousandths.
Move the point one place right: 5.
Move the point two places right: 250.
Move the point two places left: 0.36.

questions.q: In 5.678, what is the value of the digit 6?
questions.explanation: 6 is in the tenths place, so it stands for 0.6.

questions.q: A pen is 0.25 m long. Four pens placed end to end measure how long?
10 identical books cost ₹450. What is the cost of one book?

questions.explanation: Move the point two places left: 0.056.
